QUOTE: It installs its own functions by calling `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator's init function (`mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init`) installs itself via the runtime setter. It never says "only in-tree user", but it presents the allocator as "the built-in example of substitution" and the setter's only named library-internal user.
